name: pam-reattach
description: PAM module for reattaching to the user's GUI (Aqua) session

repo.name: pam_reattach
repo.description: Reattach to the user's GUI session on macOS during authentication (for Touch ID support in tmux)

readme.summary: Excellent documentation with clear purpose, comprehensive installation options, and detailed usage instructions, though troubleshooting could be more extensive.
readme.top_issue: Troubleshooting section is missing - only mentions potential bugs generically but doesn't document common problems like permission errors, file path issues, or how to verify the module is working correctly.

injection_risks.description: The execvp function is used with user-controlled input (argv[optind]) which can lead to command injection attacks if not properly sanitized.
The getenv function is used with a predefined list of environment variables, but it's still possible for an attacker to manipulate these variables.

critical_findings: Potential environment variable manipulation in src/pam.c
security.summary: The code has some security concerns, including command injection and potential environment variable manipulation, but overall it appears to be well-structured and follows good practices.

common_complaints: Path resolution issues with Homebrew installation
Breakage on macOS Big Sur and later versions
Build failures on older macOS versions
sentiment.summary: The pam-reattach project shows clear signs of abandonment with unresolved architectural compatibility issues, no maintainer responses, and a 4+ year gap between the oldest and most recent issue suggesting the project is no longer actively maintained.

communication.summary: The maintainer's responses are clear, helpful, and patient. They provide technical depth and encourage new contributors.
